questions.text: How many moles are present in 22 g of carbon(IV) oxide? [C = 12, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of CO₂ = 44 g/mol, so n = 22/44 = 0.5 mol.

questions.text: What is the electronic configuration of the sodium ion, Na⁺? [Na: Z = 11]
questions.explanation: Sodium loses its single 3s electron to form Na⁺, leaving the neon configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶.

questions.text: Which of the following is an amphoteric oxide?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis, which is the definition of an amphoteric oxide.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain has four carbons with a methyl branch at position 2, giving 2-methylbutane.

questions.text: What is the oxidation number of manganese in KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: K is +1 and each O is −2: +1 + x + 4(−2) = 0, so x = +7.

questions.text: Which gas turns lime water milky?
questions.explanation: CO₂ forms insoluble calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) with lime water, producing the milky appearance.

questions.text: How many molecules are contained in 0.5 mole of a gas? [Avogadro's number = 6.02 × 10²³]
A solution of pH 3 is
questions.explanation: Any pH below 7 is acidic, and pH 3 indicates a fairly high hydrogen ion concentration.

questions.text: During electrolysis, the reaction that occurs at the cathode is
questions.explanation: Cations migrate to the cathode and gain electrons, so reduction takes place there.

questions.text: Isotopes of an element have the same
options: mass number but different atomic numbers
atomic number but different mass numbers
number of neutrons but different protons
number of nucleons but different electrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes differ only in neutron count, so the atomic number is the same while the mass number varies.

questions.text: Temporary hardness in water is caused by the presence of
questions.explanation: Hydrogentrioxocarbonates(IV) of calcium and magnesium decompose on boiling, which is why the hardness is temporary.

questions.text: Which homologous series has the general formula CₙH₂ₙ?
questions.explanation: Alkenes contain one carbon–carbon double bond and follow CₙH₂ₙ.

questions.text: The catalyst used in the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia is
questions.explanation: Finely divided iron with promoters catalyses the combination of nitrogen and hydrogen.

questions.text: In the Contact process, sulphur(IV) oxide is oxidised to sulphur(VI) oxide using
questions.explanation: V₂O₅ is the catalyst for the conversion of SO₂ to SO₃ in the Contact process.

questions.text: Using the equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, what volume of oxygen is required to burn 10 cm³ of hydrogen completely at s.t.p.?
questions.explanation: By Gay-Lussac's law the volumes are in the ratio 2 : 1, so 10 cm³ of hydrogen needs 5 cm³ of oxygen.

questions.text: The reaction between an acid and a base to form salt and water only is called
questions.explanation: Neutralisation is the reaction of H⁺ from the acid with OH⁻ from the base to produce water and a salt.

questions.text: The rusting of iron requires the presence of
questions.explanation: Rusting is the oxidation of iron in the presence of both air (oxygen) and moisture.

questions.text: What is the molar concentration of a solution containing 0.1 mole of solute in 500 cm³ of solution?
questions.explanation: 500 cm³ = 0.5 dm³, so concentration = 0.1/0.5 = 0.2 mol/dm³.

questions.text: The ideal gas equation is expressed as
questions.explanation: The general gas equation combines Boyle's, Charles' and Avogadro's laws as PV = nRT.

questions.text: Which of the following elements is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Argon is in Group 0 with a stable octet, making it chemically inert.

questions.text: Starch is confirmed in a food sample when iodine solution gives a
questions.explanation: Iodine forms a blue-black complex with starch; brick-red is Benedict's test for reducing sugar and purple is Biuret for protein.

questions.text: Boyle's law states that at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is
questions.explanation: At constant temperature PV is constant, so V ∝ 1/P.

questions.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of H₂SO₄. [H = 1, S = 32, O = 16]
The functional group present in alkanols is
questions.explanation: Alkanols (alcohols) are characterised by the hydroxyl group, −OH.

questions.text: The change of a solid directly into vapour without passing through the liquid state is called
questions.explanation: Sublimation is shown by substances such as iodine, ammonium chloride and solid CO₂.

questions.text: In the reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, zinc acts as
questions.explanation: Zinc gives up electrons and is itself oxidised, so it reduces the copper ions and acts as the reducing agent.

questions.text: The bleaching action of chlorine water is due to
questions.explanation: Chlorine water contains HOCl (chloric(I) acid), which releases nascent oxygen and bleaches by oxidation.

questions.text: What is the formula of aluminium tetraoxosulphate(VI)?
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ and SO₄²⁻ combine in the ratio 2 : 3 to balance the charges.

questions.text: The unusually high boiling point of water compared with other hydrides of Group VI is due to
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules require extra energy to break, raising the boiling point.

questions.text: Cracking of petroleum fractions produces
questions.explanation: Cracking breaks long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter alkanes and useful alkenes such as ethene.
